title: Baursak (Kazakh fried dough puffs)
steps: Mix the yeast and sugar with the warm milk and leave for 5 minutes.
Stir in the egg, melted butter and salt, then add the flour and knead into a soft, elastic dough.
Cover and leave in a warm place for about 1 hour until doubled.
Roll the dough out 1 cm thick and cut into diamonds or squares of about 4 cm.
Heat the oil to about 170 C (340 F) and fry the pieces in small batches for 2 to 3 minutes, turning, until they puff up and turn golden brown.
Drain on paper towels. Serve warm with tea, honey or sour cream, or alongside soups and stews.

title: Beshbarmak (boiled meat with broad noodles and onion broth)

ingredients.name: beef or lamb on the bone (shank, brisket or ribs)
onions, 2 left whole and 2 sliced into thin half rings
salt and black pepper to taste

steps: Put the meat in a large pot with the 3 litres of water, bring slowly to a boil and skim off the foam. Add the bay leaves, peppercorns, whole onions and salt, then cover and simmer for 2 to 2.5 hours until the meat is very tender.
Meanwhile make the dough: mix the flour, eggs, 100 ml of water and a pinch of salt into a firm dough, knead until smooth, and rest it under a cloth for 30 minutes.
Roll the dough out very thin and cut it into large rough squares or diamonds, about 7 cm wide.
Lift the meat out of the broth, strain the broth and keep it hot. Cut the meat into slices or bite-size pieces, discarding the bones.
Pour the sliced onions into a ladleful of hot broth and simmer for 5 minutes until soft but not mushy.
Boil the noodle squares in the strained broth for 5 to 7 minutes until tender, then lift them out and spread them on a large platter.
Pile the meat over the noodles, top with the stewed onions and herbs, and serve with bowls of the hot broth for sipping.

title: Kazakh laghman (beef noodle stew with peppers)

ingredients.name: fresh or dried wheat noodles (thick spaghetti works)
tomatoes, chopped, or 2 tbsp tomato paste
salt, black pepper and fresh cilantro, to taste

steps: Heat the oil in a deep pan and fry the beef in batches over high heat until well browned.
Add the onions, carrots and peppers and cook for 5 minutes, then stir in the garlic, cumin and tomatoes or tomato paste.
Pour in the stock, season, cover and simmer for 40 to 50 minutes until the meat is tender and the sauce is thick.
Cook the noodles in plenty of boiling salted water until just tender, then drain.
Divide the noodles among bowls and ladle the meat and vegetable sauce on top. Scatter with cilantro and black pepper.

title: Kazakh manti (large steamed meat dumplings)

ingredients.name: beef or lamb, hand-chopped or coarsely minced
beef or lamb fat, finely diced (or butter)
sour cream or yogurt, to serve

steps: Knead the flour, water and salt into a firm dough, cover and rest for 30 minutes.
Mix the meat, onions, fat, pepper and salt well. The raw onion gives the filling its juice.
Roll the dough thin and cut into 10 cm squares.
Put a heaped spoonful of filling in the middle of each square, bring the four corners to the centre and pinch together, or fold into a half-moon shape.
Grease the tiers of a steamer and arrange the manti with space between them.
Steam over boiling water for 40 to 45 minutes until the dough is translucent and the filling is cooked.
Serve hot with sour cream or yogurt.

title: Kazakh palau (beef and carrot pilaf)

ingredients.name: beef or lamb, cut into chunks
garlic, whole, outer papery layers removed

steps: Heat the oil in a heavy pot until it shimmers and brown the meat on all sides.
Add the onions and fry until deep golden, then add the carrots and cook for 5 more minutes, stirring.
Pour in the hot water, add the cumin and salt, and simmer, covered, for 30 to 40 minutes until the meat is nearly tender.
Spread the rice evenly over the meat and vegetables without stirring. Press the whole garlic head into the middle.
Add just enough hot water to cover the rice by about 1 cm, bring to a boil, then lower the heat, cover and cook for 20 minutes until the rice is tender and the liquid is gone.
Stir gently, pile onto a platter and serve with the meat and garlic on top.

title: Kazakh samsa (baked beef and onion pastries)

ingredients.name: beef (or lamb), cut into very small cubes

steps: Knead the flour, water and salt into a firm dough. Roll it out into a rectangle, spread with the softened butter, fold up like an envelope, then roll again. Repeat twice, then chill for 30 minutes.
Mix the beef, onions, fat, cumin, salt and black pepper to make a juicy filling.
Roll out the dough thinly and cut into 12 cm squares.
Place a generous spoonful of filling in the centre of each, fold the corners to the middle to make a square or triangular parcel, and pinch the seams firmly.
Place seam-side down on a lined tray, brush with egg yolk and scatter with sesame seeds.
Bake at 200 C (400 F) for 15 minutes, then lower to 180 C (350 F) for another 25 minutes until golden and the meat is cooked through.

title: Kespe (Kazakh hand-cut noodle soup)

ingredients.name: lamb or beef on the bone

steps: Simmer the meat in the water for 1 hour with salt, skimming, until tender. Remove the meat, cut it up and return it to the broth.
Mix the flour, eggs, salt and about 3 tablespoons of cold water into a stiff dough. Knead and rest it for 20 minutes.
Roll the dough out very thin, dust it with flour, fold it and cut it into fine noodles, or into small squares.
Add the onion, potatoes and carrot to the broth and simmer for 15 minutes.
Drop in the noodles and cook for 5 to 7 minutes until tender.
Serve in bowls with plenty of dill and a spoonful of sour cream if you like.

title: Kuurdak (Kazakh pan-fried meat and offal)

ingredients.name: beef or lamb, with some fat, cut into small cubes
beef or lamb liver and heart, cubed (optional but traditional)

steps: Heat the oil or fat in a deep skillet or cast-iron pot until hot, then brown the cubes of meat for 10 to 15 minutes until golden and the fat has rendered.
Add the heart and cook for 5 minutes, then add the liver and cook just until it loses its raw colour, about 3 more minutes.
Add the onions and fry until soft and lightly browned, then season with salt and pepper.
In a separate pan, fry the potatoes in a little oil until golden and cooked through, then add them to the meat. (Some cooks stir the raw potatoes in and cover the pot for 15 minutes instead.)
Stir everything together over medium heat for a few more minutes so the flavours meld, then scatter with fresh herbs.
Serve hot, straight from the pan, with flatbread and pickled vegetables.

title: Naryn (Kazakh sliced boiled meat and hand-cut noodles with onion)

ingredients.name: beef or lamb on the bone

steps: Simmer the meat in the water with a little salt for 2 hours until tender, skimming off the foam.
Make a firm dough from the flour, egg, water and a pinch of salt, rest for 20 minutes, then roll it out thin.
Cut the dough into long thin noodles and boil them in salted water until tender, about 3 to 4 minutes. Drain and let them dry slightly.
Remove the meat from the broth and shred or cut it into thin strips.
Mix the meat, noodles and onion in a bowl, season generously with pepper and add a few ladles of the hot broth to moisten.
Top with herbs and serve with a bowl of the broth on the side.

title: Nauryz kozhe (Kazakh spring grain and meat soup for Nauryz)
steps: Bring the meat and water to a boil in a large pot, skim, add the onion and simmer for 1 hour.
Add the wheat or barley and carrot and simmer for another 30 minutes.
Stir in the millet and rice and cook for 20 to 25 minutes until all grains are soft and the soup is thick.
Lift out the meat, cut it into small pieces and return it to the pot.
Pour in the milk, season with salt and heat gently for 5 minutes without boiling hard.
Serve hot in bowls. Traditionally this soup is made with seven ingredients to mark the new year.

title: Qattama (Kazakh layered fried flatbread)
steps: Knead the flour, water and salt into a soft dough and rest it for 30 minutes.
Divide into 6 pieces and roll each as thinly as you can into a long strip.
Brush each strip with melted butter, then roll it up into a tight coil like a snail and let it rest for 10 minutes.
Flatten each coil gently with the palm and roll into a round about 18 cm wide.
Cook in a lightly oiled heavy pan over medium heat for 3 to 4 minutes per side until golden and flaky.
Pinch it between your hands as it comes off the pan to loosen the layers, and serve warm.

title: Shelpek (Kazakh fried flatbreads)

ingredients.name: sunflower or vegetable oil, for shallow frying

steps: Stir the yeast, sugar and salt into the warm milk and leave for 5 minutes until it foams a little.
Add the flour and knead into a soft dough, then cover and let it rest for 30 to 40 minutes.
Divide into 10 to 12 pieces and roll each into a thin round about 15 cm wide. Prick them all over with a fork so they do not puff up too much.
Heat about 2 cm of oil in a wide pan over medium-high heat. Fry each flatbread for about 1 minute per side until golden and blistered.
Drain on paper towels and serve warm with tea, jam or soup.

title: Sorpa (Kazakh meat broth with herbs)

ingredients.name: lamb or beef on the bone
salt and black pepper to taste

steps: Put the meat in a large pot with the water and a pinch of salt. Bring to a boil, skim and simmer for 1.5 hours.
Add the whole onion and carrots and cook for another 20 minutes.
Add the potatoes, tomatoes, pepper and sliced onion and simmer for 25 minutes more until everything is soft.
Taste and season with salt and pepper.
Serve in deep bowls with the meat on the bone, a scattering of herbs and flatbread.
